pages.title: Implementation: Traversal, Filtering, Formatting, and Errors
pages.purpose: Source-grounded explanation of how files_to_prompt/cli.py walks inputs, handles hidden files and .gitignore rules, formats the three output styles, handles errors, plus a focused maintenance guide grounded in the implementation and the pytest suite.
instructions: Cover: input traversal via os.walk and per-directory filtering order (hidden, gitignore, ignore patterns, extensions), how .gitignore rules accumulate (top-level dirname plus each walked root) and how should_ignore fnmatches basenames, the three writers (default, cxml with global index, markdown with EXT_TO_LANG and adaptive backtick fences), add_line_numbers padding, error handling (UnicodeDecodeError warning to stderr with exit 0, BadArgumentUsage for missing paths, click Path exists=True for arguments), and a short maintenance guide: how to add an extension/language, how to extend ignore semantics, and how to add and run tests (CliRunner patterns, pytest via .[test] extra, CI matrix).
Do not document OpenWiki-generated integration files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, openwiki-update workflow).
Ground every non-obvious technical claim in files_to_prompt/cli.py and tests/test_files_to_prompt.py, citing repo:// spans where useful.
Keep the page between 400 and 600 words.
State uncertainty when evidence is absent rather than inventing behavior.
